## Package updates bump and fix, never skip

`routines/package-updates.md` (0.27.0) held back any package whose bump broke a gate. The owner's rule is the
opposite: a bump that breaks a gate is still made, and the project is adapted in the same pull request.

- Hard rule 3 is now **"Bump and fix, never skip"**: the run adapts the project (code, config, messages,
  migrations, regenerated files) in the same pull request and adds tests that prove the adapted behaviour, each
  seen red without the fix and recorded in `## Progress`.
- A break the release notes do not explain is investigated (the package's source and tests at the new tag) and
  adapted to, not skipped.
- A package is held back (`routines.packageUpdates.hold`, an issue in its owning repository) only for a defect in
  the package itself that the project could fix only by patching or wrapping SOFTURE code.

Adopting projects pick it up with the next bump: their routine reads the shipped file.
